new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..b10130b593
--- /dev/null

+# 2011 April 22
+#
+# The author disclaims copyright to this source code.  In place of
+# a legal notice, here is a blessing:

+#    May you do good and not evil.

+
+set testdir [file dirname $argv0]
+source $testdir/tester.tcl
+
+set testprefix uri
+db close
+
+sqlite3_shutdown
+sqlite3_config_uri 1
+
+#-------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Test that file names are correctly extracted from URIs.
+#
+foreach {tn uri file} {
+  1      test.db                            test.db
+  2      file:test.db                       test.db
+  3      file://an-authorityPWD/test.db     test.db
+  4      file:PWD/test.db                   test.db
+  5      file:test.db?mork=1                test.db
+  6      file:test.db?mork=1&tonglor=2      test.db
+  7      file:test.db?mork=1#boris          test.db
+  8      file:test.db#boris                 test.db
+  9      test.db#boris                      test.db#boris
+  10     test.db?mork=1#boris               test.db?mork=1#boris
+  11     file:test%2Edb                     test.db
+  12     file                               file
+  13     http:test.db                       http:test.db
+} {
+  set uri  [string map [list PWD [pwd]] $uri]
+  set file [string map [list PWD [pwd]] $file]
+
+  forcedelete $file
+  do_test 1.$tn.1 { file exists $file } 0
+  set DB [sqlite3_open $uri]
+  do_test 1.$tn.2 { file exists $file } 1
+  sqlite3_close $DB
+}
+
+
+#-------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Test that URI query parameters are passed through to the VFS layer
+# correctly.
+#
+testvfs tvfs -default 1
+tvfs filter xOpen
+tvfs script open_method
+proc open_method {method file arglist} {
+  set ::arglist $arglist
+}
+breakpoint
+foreach {tn uri kvlist} {
+  1      file:test.db?hello=world              {hello world}
+  2      file:test.db?hello&world              {hello {} world {}}
+  3      file:test.db?hello=1&world=2&vfs=tvfs {hello 1 world 2 vfs tvfs}
+  4      file:test.db?hello=1&world=2&vfs=unix {}
+} {
+  set ::arglist ""
+  set DB [sqlite3_open $uri]
+  do_test 2.$tn { set ::arglist } $kvlist
+  sqlite3_close $DB
+}
+
+finish_test
+

fix_commit.message: Fix the sqlite3ParseUri() for improved defenses against ridiculously long URI inputs causing integer overflow problems. [bugs:/info/2026-06-24T11:46:39Z|Bug 2026-06-24T11:46:39Z].
fix_commit.author: drh

findings.title: Integer overflow in sqlite3ParseUri() with ridiculously long URI inputs
findings.message: In sqlite3ParseUri(), the URI length and loop indices are stored as 32-bit signed int values. `nUri` is computed via `sqlite3Strlen30(zUri)`, which silently caps the result at 0x3fffffff (~1 GB) for longer inputs. The loop variables `iIn` and `iOut` are also `int`, so for a URI longer than ~2 GB they will overflow from positive to negative (signed integer overflow, undefined behavior in C), allowing `iOut` to point before the start of the allocated `zFile` buffer and causing an out-of-bounds write. Even in the sub-2GB range, the truncated `nUri` causes `nByte = nUri+8` to under-allocate relative to the true string length, enabling a heap buffer overflow as `iOut` writes beyond the buffer boundary.
findings.suggestion: Replace all int variables tracking URI/option lengths and indices (nUri, iIn, iOut, nOpt, nVal) with i64 (or sqlite3_int64), and use strlen() directly instead of sqlite3Strlen30() so that the 0x3fffffff cap is not applied. Also add an explicit cast to int where the value is passed to printf's %.*s format specifier.

ground_truth.root_cause: When the uri-filenames feature was introduced in 2011, all length and index variables in sqlite3ParseUri() were typed as 32-bit signed int using sqlite3Strlen30() (which has an implicit 1 GB cap). This was never updated to handle inputs approaching or exceeding the 32-bit int range, creating an integer overflow vulnerability for pathologically long URI strings.
